intro.title: Generic List<T>
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a reusable List component that can display items of any data type, such as strings, numbers, or custom objects. You will learn how to use TypeScript generics, denoted by <T>, to create flexible and type-safe components. The main technologies involved are React for the UI structure and TypeScript for adding static types. By the end, you'll understand how to write a single component that works with multiple data types while ensuring your code is robust and easy to maintain.
intro.usecase: Generic List<T> components are fundamental building blocks in modern React applications that handle dynamic data collections. You'll use them in e-commerce product listings where each item has different properties (name, price, rating), admin dashboards displaying user tables with varying column configurations, and content management systems showing articles with diverse metadata. This pattern allows you to create reusable, type-safe list components that adapt to different data structures while maintaining excellent developer experience through TypeScript's type checking and IntelliSense support.
